mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates accommodative monetary policy, which reduces the discount rate applied to equity cash flows, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days in any macro regime.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when FEDFUNDS is below its 3-month moving average, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 0.2 percentage points over three months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not negative in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE rises > 0.2pp in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days through improved corporate revenue outlooks.
failure_condition: The joint increase in HOUST and RSAFS does not produce positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a high inflation regime (CPIAUCSL > 195), rising inflation pressures lead to expectations of monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL > 195, the 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the average return exceeds -0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals weakening economic activity, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to deteriorating business conditions in any macro regime.
failure_condition: INDPRO decline does not lead to negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 2000.0 thousand units over two months signals a housing market downturn, which typically precedes a positive S&P 500 return over the next 20 days as the market anticipates policy stimulus.
failure_condition: When HOUST falls below 2000.0 in 2 months, the 20-day forward returns are not positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in employment (PAYEMS) and rise in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates severe labor market deterioration, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days as the economy approaches a recession.
failure_condition: The joint decline in PAYEMS and rise in UNRATE does not produce negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion (GDPC1 > 11000 billion), the S&P 500 tends to produce positive returns over the next 20 days due to sustained corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: In periods of GDPC1 > 11000, the 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the average return is below 0.5%.
